verification_scope: Claims below were checked against retrieved organizer, government, institutional or publisher pages. This is a bounded source audit, not a guarantee of zero error.

claims_verified: The target is geological fault presence, not direct geothermal-vent or reservoir labels.
DTI uses alpha 0.2, beta 0.8 and a 300 m triangular kernel.
A submission is a single float32 prediction band in EPSG:32611 at 100 m resolution, with matching training-data bounds and values between 0 and 1.
The public format description permits null/NaN outside the bounds; our all-finite export is a compatibility precaution, not proof that NaN caused the reported rejection.
One selected submission is scored across both prize rounds.
The known-fault evaluation mask is pixel-exact and identical to the provided training fault labels.
Only new-fault ground truth supplies kernel credit; proximity to known faults is not free.
New-fault ground-truth pixels can lie within 300 m of a known trace.
Any fault pixel not already captured by USGS/INGENIOUS can count as new, including newly mapped geometry of an existing fault system.
Faults are structures with displacement; a lineament alone does not establish a fault.
Geophysical and elevation information can help infer concealed structures.

sources.authority: Official GEMS Prize rules, September 2026; sections 3.2 through 3.6
claims_verified: The rules specify three submissions per week; the logged-in page remains authoritative for the team's remaining slots.
Entrants must register and accept the competition terms.
Finalists must provide reproducible code and documentation.
Generative-AI use is allowed but must be disclosed in the narrative; competitors remain responsible for accuracy and authorship.
GeoDAWN includes airborne magnetic and radiometric surveys intended to support geothermal and critical-mineral studies.
Area 2 flight lines were spaced 400 m apart at an azimuth of 90 degrees; leveling residuals are a plausible non-fault magnetic-lineament mimic.
Variable terrain clearance should be considered when interpreting the survey.
The release is marked CC0 1.0.

sources.authority: Geothermal Data Repository record for the USGS/DOE GeoDAWN survey
sources.status: catalogue metadata retrieved; exact binary asset and asset-specific license not retrieved

The linked USGS/ScienceBase record is separately recorded as CC0 1.0 in the USGS source check; the repository does not establish which license statement governs a particular future binary asset.
Exact asset availability, AOI coverage, usable-band definitions, CRS, and competition-grid alignment remain unverified.

sources.status: retrieved metadata; direct binary downloads are outside this sandbox's host allowlist
claims_verified: The official regional compilation contains quaternary-fault data and geophysical and geothermal layers.
Quaternary Faults v2 is linked publicly; its license is CC BY 4.0 with attribution.
The CSV in this repository is a third-party derivative, not an independently authenticated copy of the official shapefile.

sources.authority: Geological Society of London publisher abstract
sources.status: abstract retrieved; full article is not claimed to have been reviewed
claims_verified: Distributed dextral-shear experiments develop left-stepping en echelon Riedel shears and short synthetic linking shears.
Later fault patterns are influenced by existing master faults and local stress changes.
Fracture density decays away from the primary fault, and mature damage patterns can be represented by superposed contributions from secondary strands.
The displacement/zone-width relationship changes with fault maturity.
Mapped connected-component pixel count is only our noisy length proxy; the paper does not verify its suitability for this particular raster.

sources.authority: GSA publisher bibliographic record and indexed abstract
sources.status: title and bibliographic record verified; full article not retrieved
claims_verified: Similarities between Shear Zones of Different Magnitudes, GSA Bulletin 81, 1625-1640, is the classical shear-zone framework cited by the brief; no numerical angle is copied into the model.

sources.authority: Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology institutional publication list
sources.status: bibliography verified; no claim of a full-paper review
claims_verified: The institution lists Kinematics of the northern Walker Lane: An incipient transform fault along the Pacific-North American plate boundary, Geology 33, 505-508, by Faulds, Henry and Hinz.
The reference solution supports CPU execution; a GPU is recommended for faster neural-network training, not required for this CPU fault-zone lane.

sources.authority: Third-party construction audit, NOT organizer score confirmation
sources.status: retrieved and raster construction independently measured
claims_verified: The H33-2-B2 raster is exactly its 40199-dot base with 2545 dots at distance <=2 pixels to the supplied catalogue removed, leaving 37654 dots.
The repository explicitly labels its 0.2747 value a projection and says no organizer score exists in that audit.
The owner's supplied 0.2778 score cannot be attributed to this exact file without a submission receipt.

limitations: No DrivenData authenticated session, private labels, submission-page receipt or remaining-slot counter is available.
Sandbox binary egress is restricted to GitHub and package hosts; official pages were reviewed with the page-retrieval tool.
No inference about geothermal heat, flow, reservoir volume or economic viability is licensed by a fault-probability raster alone.
The two-hour / three-experiment research budget limits geological validation.
